Action Plan:
1) Acute left-sided headache since early morning today:
   - Start ibuprofen as first-line analgesic for suspected migraine; patient may continue paracetamol if desired. Doses/route/frequency not documented.
   - First-line options discussed included ibuprofen or aspirin; aspirin not specifically initiated. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
   - Encourage rest, hydration (1.5–2 L fluids/day excluding caffeinated drinks), and adequate sleep (7–8 hours nightly).
   - Provide written safety-net advice with danger signs for headaches; advise low threshold to contact GP/urgent care if symptoms worsen or new red flags occur.
2) Work-related stress and history of anxiety on sertraline:
   - Consider 1 week off work (self-certify) to reduce stress.
   - Provide link to local counseling service for self-referral; encourage use.
   - Continue current sertraline (dose not documented); no change today.
3) Follow-up:
   - Book follow-up in 1 week to reassess headache response and overall status.
   - If not improving, consider further evaluation including blood tests and other investigations as indicated.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: New severe left-sided headache that woke patient at ~05:30 today; still present.
- Symptom details:
  - Acute onset; more severe than prior headaches.
  - Unilateral (left) this time; prior headaches typically frontal/bilateral “cluster” sensation (patient’s wording).
  - Mild photophobia; tolerable.
  - No nausea/vomiting. Brief dizziness on awakening resolved.
  - No neck stiffness; no fever.
  - Lying down initially uncomfortable but ultimately improves pain.
  - Paracetamol taken this morning with no benefit.
- Past medical history: Anxiety (~2 years). History of headaches (less severe, usually frontal/bilateral). No known hypertension; BP never checked.
- Medications: Sertraline (ongoing; dose not documented). Paracetamol taken today (dose not documented).
- Family history: Mother with anxiety. No known family history of migraine.
- Social history: Work-related stress and late nights for ~2 months. Lives with partner. Non-smoker. Runs ~3x/week. Has a cat. Diet “okay.”
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- Telemedicine consultation; no vitals or physical exam performed.
- Patient reports:
  - No fever.
  - No neck stiffness.
  - No focal neurological symptoms reported (no visual changes reported).
  - Mild photophobia present.
- Investigations: None today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute left-sided headache:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Migraine without aura (High likelihood per DDx).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     • Tension-type headache (Medium likelihood) — stress and prior frontal headaches support; unilateral severe pain and photophobia oppose.  
     • Cluster headache (Low-Medium) — early morning unilateral pain supports; lack of autonomic features and relief with lying down oppose.  
     • Spontaneous intracranial hypotension (Low) — improves when lying down supports; onset in sleep and no upright worsening oppose.  
     • Secondary headache due to intracranial mass/raised ICP (Low) — “woke from sleep” is a red flag; improvement when lying down and no neuro deficits oppose.
   - Investigations planned: None immediately. If not improving at 1-week follow-up, consider blood tests and further evaluation per GP assessment.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Start ibuprofen as first-line for migraine-type headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
     • May continue paracetamol; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
     • First-line option of aspirin discussed but not initiated; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
     • Lifestyle: ensure 1.5–2 L fluids/day (non-caffeinated) and 7–8 hours sleep nightly; rest.
     • Safety-net: provide written danger signs for headaches; seek urgent care if worsening, new neuro deficits, severe “worst-ever” headache, persistent vomiting, fever/neck stiffness, visual changes, or other concerning features.
   - Relevant referrals: None immediate.

2. Work-related stress and anxiety on sertraline:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Work-related stress; anxiety disorder on stable sertraline. No suicidal ideation disclosed.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: None today.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Encourage taking 1 week off work (self-certify) to reduce stress.  
     • Sleep hygiene and hydration as above.  
     • Continue sertraline (dose not documented); no change discussed today.
   - Relevant referrals: Provide link for local counseling service; patient to self-refer.

3. Follow-up and safety-netting:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Monitoring for headache course and response to initial management.
   - Differential diagnosis: As above for headache; reassess if new features arise.
   - Investigations planned: Consider blood tests and other investigations if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment planned: Reassess analgesia efficacy; adjust plan based on response and any new findings.
   - Relevant referrals: As needed based on reassessment.

  • No vital signs or neurological examination performed (telemedicine limitations).  
  • Blood pressure not measured today.  
  • Analgesic dosing/route/frequency not documented.  
  • No screening documented for NSAID contraindications (e.g., peptic ulcer disease, renal disease, anticoagulants) before starting ibuprofen.  
  • Migraine features (aura, activity limitation, phonophobia) not fully characterized.
- Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.
